body:
## What happens

A task that ends `failed` with its work still held keeps wearing `your call` and keeps counting toward `needs you`, for the rest of the session, with no way to reach zero except answering each one.

`internal/session/task_status.go:441`:

```go
case TaskFailed:
	if facts.Held {
		// THE ANSWER IS STILL THERE AND SOMEBODY MAY STILL WANT IT...
		status.Presence, status.On = TaskPresenceNeedsLook, TaskWaitPerson
		return status
	}
```

The offer is real — the branch is on disk and taking it anyway is a genuine answer. The problem is that the offer never expires.

## What it looks like

One session, 23 nodes. Four rows stand in `needs you`, all `state=failed`, `ending=refused`, `merge=aborted`, each with a kept branch that exists:

| node | title | branch |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Skills: five-part record and store serving | `task/skills-five-part-record-and-stor-…` |
| 6 | Skills: chat shelf and use_skill tool | `task/skills-chat-shelf-and-use-skill-…` |
| 7 | Store skill fact fields | `task/store-skill-fact-fields-…` |
| 15 | File GitHub issue: standing firing sees empty task board | `task/file-github-issue-standing-firin-…` |

By the time they were read, the conversation had moved two tranches past them: a later node had already landed a continuation of the same store-record branch, none of the four branches had ever been pushed, and nothing in flight was waiting on any of them. The count said four people-shaped questions. Zero of them were blocking anything.

## Why it is wrong

A mark exists only when a person's answer is the one thing unblocking the work. A card may keep showing a state; a mark must not. A mark is a demand and a card is a status. Four standing demands that unblock nothing train a person to stop reading the count, which costs the marks that do matter.

## Shape of the fix

A held landing is a question while the conversation is still on it, and a status afterwards. When the work has been superseded, or the session has moved past it, the row keeps its branch and its offer on the card and stops wearing the mark and stops counting toward `needs you`.

Open question for whoever takes it: what "moved past it" should be measured against. Candidates seen here — a later node that landed the same branch, a node whose branch no longer exists, and plain distance in the graph. The first two are facts already on the record; the third is a guess. Pick from the record, not the clock.

## Not this

The four rows are not stale state, not a cache, and not a surface drawing something the engine did not say. This was checked: the engine was restarted onto the current build first, the records were read off disk, and the rows are what `ProjectTask` returns for those facts. The reading is correct. The demand is what is wrong.
